open_decision: The laws do not decide whether a release by the owner clears the owner record and the critical-section flag, so a design may ignore the owner's release.
input: [spawn 5, acquire 5, release 5], with the owner process at pid 5 and token 0
result_a: Design A (the Solution lock, isOwner r p = decide (r = p)): after the release, process <5,0> is not in the critical section (cs = false).
result_b: Design B (the same lock with isOwner r p = false, so a release never matches the owner): after the release, process <5,0> is still in the critical section (cs = true).
reason: Design B passes Mutex, NoOrphanHold, HolderKeepsLock, CanRefuse and CanEnter: the owner stays live until it exits, so grants stays false while the holder is alive, and only release or exit clears cs, with release never clearing it in B. The laws never require a release to free the lock, so the two designs differ on cs for process <5,0>.
